The push token request is not guarded, so a failure stops the permission step.

terms.meaning: a message the server sends that appears on the phone, even when the app is closed.
an address that tells the push service where to deliver messages for this phone.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and display rules
sections.what: Sets how notifications appear while the app is open: they show an alert, play a sound and update the badge.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes reminders visible even when the app is in use.
sections.watch_out: This setting applies when the file loads, so the file must be loaded early enough to take effect.

sections.name: REMINDER_ACTIONS
sections.title: Reminder button IDs
sections.what: Names the three buttons on a medicine reminder: taken, snooze and skip.
sections.why: Gives each button a fixed ID so the tap handler can tell them apart.
sections.watch_out: These IDs must match the buttons registered in init. Renaming one in only one place breaks that button silently.

sections.name: NotificationManager (part 1)
sections.title: Reminder buttons and tap listener
sections.what: Registers the three reminder buttons and listens for taps. Taken and skip record the answer on the server, snooze asks the server to snooze, and a plain tap opens the home screen with the reminder. Taps without a log ID are ignored.
sections.why: Likely reason: the skip button is marked destructive, which on iOS shows it in red.
sections.watch_out: Each call to init adds another listener, so calling it more than once can handle one tap several times.

sections.name: NotificationManager: if
sections.title: Permission, device registration and Android channel
sections.what: Asks for notification permission if needed, gets the device push token, sends it to the server with a device type and name, and on Android creates a loud channel with vibration. Returns true if permission was granted, otherwise false.
sections.why: Likely reason: the server needs the push token to send notifications to this phone.
sections.watch_out: The token request is not inside the error handling, so a failure there stops the step. Device names are simple guesses, such as iPhone or Android Device.

summary: Sets up push notifications: reminder buttons, tap handling, permission request and device registration.
purpose: Lets a user take, snooze or skip a medicine reminder from the notification, and sends the phone's push address to the server.
why: Likely reason: lets the user act on reminders without opening the app.
how: When the file loads, sets how notifications appear while the app is open. init registers the reminder buttons and a listener for taps. requestPermissions asks for permission, gets the push token, sends it to the server, and on Android creates the default channel.
inputs: Notification taps with a log ID, the user's permission answer, and the device push token.
outputs: Server calls to record a response, snooze, or register the device; navigation to the home screen on a plain tap; true or false from the permission step.
risks: Calling init more than once adds more listeners, so one tap can be handled several times. The token request is outside the error handling. Device names are guesses. Failed reminder responses are only logged.
debug: If reminder buttons do nothing, check that the button IDs match and that the notification carries a log ID. If no push arrives, check that permission returned true and look for registration errors in the log. Check device logs for token errors.
